intro.title: Text 1 · A New Routine
intro.scene: Emma writes about her new life in London.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Hi! I'm Emma. I've lived in London for a few months now, and my life is quite different.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: I usually get up at seven and have breakfast before I leave home. I take the bus to work three days a week. On other days, I study English and work on my own projects.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: At the moment, I'm preparing for a new English course. I'm also looking for a new flat because my current room is quite small.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: My friends Oliver and Sophie are helping me. Oliver knows a lot about London, and Sophie is always finding interesting places to visit.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Life in a big city isn't always easy, but I'm learning something new every day. I'm excited about this new chapter!

intro.title: Text 2 · Catching Up
intro.scene: Emma, Oliver and Sophie meet in a café.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Emma! It's good to see you again. How's everything going?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Pretty well, thanks! I'm really busy these days.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Really? What are you doing?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: I'm working part-time, and I'm studying English. I'm also looking for a bigger flat.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: That's exciting! Do you still live near the park?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Yes, I do, but I want to move closer to work.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: I understand. I usually cycle to work, but this week I'm taking the bus because my bike isn't working.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: I'm taking a photography course at the moment. It's great fun!

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: That sounds interesting! Are you enjoying it?

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Yes, I am. I meet interesting people every week.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: We all have something new to talk about!

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Exactly! And our English course starts again soon.

sections.title: 1.1 Present Simple – građenje i nastavci
sections.explanation:
Present Simple koristimo za navike, rutine, opšte činjenice, relativno stalna stanja i događaje prema utvrđenom rasporedu.
Obrazac: SUBJEKAT + GLAGOL (he / she / it + -s). Odrični: don't / doesn't + glagol. Upitni: Do / Does + subjekat + glagol?
table: I don't work. · Do you work?
She doesn't work. · Does she work?
rules: Posle -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -z i kod go/do dodajemo -es: watch → watches, go → goes
Posle doesn't / does glagol nema -s: She doesn't work. Does she work?
sections.compare: Glagol to be ne koristi do/does: She is happy. → She isn't happy. → Is she happy? Ne kažemo „Does she be happy?”.
examples: Da li Sophie živi u Londonu?
We don't have classes on Fridays.
mistakes: Posle doesn't glagol je u osnovnom obliku.
sections.remember: he / she / it → glagol + -s; pitanja i negacija → do / does + osnovni glagol.

sections.title: 1.2 Prilozi učestalosti i vremenski izrazi
sections.explanation: Uz Present Simple često stoje reči koje pokazuju koliko često se nešto dešava. Prilozi učestalosti obično stoje ISPRED glavnog glagola, ali POSLE glagola to be.
table: every day, once a week, twice a month
examples: I usually go to work by bus.
mistakes: I go usually to work by bus.
I usually go to work by bus.
Uz to be prilog stoji posle glagola.
sections.remember: Prilog ispred glavnog glagola, a posle am / is / are.

sections.title: 2.1 Present Continuous – građenje i -ing
sections.explanation:
Present Continuous koristimo za radnju koja traje u trenutku govora, privremenu situaciju ili promenu koja se odvija.
Obrazac: SUBJEKAT + AM / IS / ARE + GLAGOL-ING.
table: Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.
rules: Kratak naglašen samoglasnik + suglasnik: udvajanje → sit → sitting, run → running
Ne udvajamo svaki suglasnik: open → opening, visit → visiting
examples: Emma is talking to Sophie right now.
Emma upravo sada razgovara sa Sophie.
sections.remember: am / is / are + glagol-ing — bez pomoćnog glagola nema Continuous-a.

sections.title: 2.2 Kada koristimo Present Continuous?
sections.explanation:
Četiri glavne upotrebe:
1. Radnja se odvija upravo sada.
2. Privremena situacija.
3. Promena ili razvoj.
4. Dogovorena bliska budućnost (kratko podsećanje; detaljnije u kasnijoj lekciji).
Važno: vremenski izrazi su tragovi, a ne automatska pravila.
table: We're having lunch at the moment.
Oliver is currently looking for a job.
Emma is taking a new course this month.
I'm learning a lot these days.
She's staying with a friend for the time being.
We're preparing for the exam at present.
examples: I'm staying with my aunt this week.
Sutra se nalazimo sa Ms Taylor (dogovoreno).
sections.remember: Sada, privremeno, promena, dogovor → Present Continuous.

sections.title: 3.1 Present Simple vs. Present Continuous
sections.explanation:
Ovo je centralna gramatička oblast lekcije: vreme biramo prema značenju i kontekstu.
Postavi sebi tri pitanja:
1. Da li je to navika ili redovna činjenica? → Present Simple.
2. Da li se radnja odvija sada ili je situacija privremena? → Present Continuous.
3. Da li glagol opisuje stanje, osećanje, posedovanje ili znanje? → Proveri stative verbs.
table: I'm working from home this week.
Emma takes the bus to work.
Emma is walking to work today.
Oliver is studying for a test right now.
Sophie is staying with a friend this month.
I usually get up at seven.
I'm getting up earlier this week.
We have English classes twice a week.
We're having an extra class today.
She's working on a new project.
We're meeting the teacher at six.
sections.compare: U srpskom prezent pokriva oba značenja, a razliku pravimo prilozima i kontekstom („svaki dan učim” / „trenutno učim”). Engleski razliku pokazuje oblikom glagola.
examples: I'm studying English at the moment.
I'm staying with a friend these days.
mistakes: I am living in London since 2010.
She is going to the gym every day.
She goes to the gym every day.
sections.remember: Navika i činjenica → Simple; sada i privremeno → Continuous.

sections.title: 4.1 Stative verbs – šta su i glavne kategorije
sections.explanation:
Stative verbs označavaju stanje, mišljenje, osećanje, posedovanje ili opažanje, a ne aktivnost. Zato ih u tim značenjima koristimo u Present Simple, čak i kada govorimo o sadašnjem trenutku.
Na A2 nivou najvažniji su: like, know, want, need, understand, have i think.
table: want, need, like, love, hate, prefer
examples: Da li se sećaš njegovog imena?
sections.compare: U srpskom kažemo „Sada razumem”, ali to ne znači Continuous u engleskom: Now I understand. Reči now i at the moment ne zahtevaju automatski Present Continuous: I want to go home now. I know the answer now.
mistakes: Now ne menja pravilo za need.
sections.remember: Znanje, želje, osećanja, posedovanje → Present Simple, i kad je „sada”.

sections.title: 4.2 Glagoli koji mogu biti stative i action
sections.explanation:
Neki glagoli stoje u oba vremena, ali tada imaju različito značenje. Za ovu lekciju najvažniji su think i have; ostali su korisna napomena.
Napomena: u neformalnom engleskom čuje se i „I'm loving it”, ali za A2 važi osnovno pravilo – like / love / prefer u Present Simple.
table: I think this is a good idea. – Mislim da je ovo dobra ideja.
I'm thinking about moving. – Razmišljam o selidbi.
I have a car. – Imam automobil.
I see the bus. – Vidim autobus.
I'm seeing my doctor tomorrow. – Sutra imam pregled.
The soup tastes good. – Supa ima dobar ukus.
I'm tasting the soup. – Probam supu.
Oliver is friendly. – Oliver je ljubazan.
Oliver is being very quiet today. – Danas se ponaša neobično tiho.
sections.remember: think = mišljenje (Simple) / razmišljanje (Continuous); have = posedovanje (Simple) / aktivnost (Continuous).

texts.title: Text 1 · A Busy Week
texts.body:
Emma has a busy week. She works part-time at a bookshop on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. She usually gets up at seven, has breakfast, and catches the bus to work.

On Tuesdays and Thursdays, she attends her English course in the evening, so she studies at home in the afternoon. This week is a little different because she is preparing for a class presentation. She is also looking for a new flat, so she spends time online after dinner.

On Saturday, she tidies her room, does the laundry, and meets up with Sophie for coffee. On Sunday, she goes for a walk with Oliver and plans the new week.

texts.title: Text 2 · A Message from Sophie
texts.body:
Hi Emma!
Sorry, I can't meet you on Friday evening because I'm helping my cousin move to a new flat. I'm busy on Saturday morning too, because I'm taking my bike to the repair shop. But I'm free in the afternoon. Do you want to meet at the café near the park at 4 p.m.? We can talk about your English course and your flat search. Oliver wants to join us later, after his photography class. Let me know if the plan works for you!

texts.title: Text 3 · A New Start in London
texts.body:
When Lucas moved to London two months ago, everything felt new and a little confusing. Back home, he lived in a small town and knew everyone. In London, life is faster, the buses are always busy, and people seem to be in a hurry.

At first, Lucas found it difficult to get used to his new routine. He started a new job in a hotel, worked different shifts, and spent his evenings studying English. He also wanted to make new friends, so he joined a local football group on Sundays.

Little by little, things became easier. He learned how to manage his time, found a nice café near his flat, and began to enjoy the city. These days, he still misses his family, but he feels more confident and comfortable in his new life.
